summary: A hand-cut tunnel and a suspension bridge lead to the Golden Gate's northern light, where the 1855 Fresnel lens moved down the cliff in 1877 to get under the fog.

structures.note: Original 1855 tower on the hill (56 ft conical brick per LighthouseFriends); lantern room and lens moved 1877 to a new brick base at the tip of the point

access.note: Trail open third Saturday monthly 12:30-3:30 p.m. (NPS); suspension bridge closed since August 2024; tower not open.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (light); National Park Service (Golden Gate National Recreation Area)

evidence.supports: Coast Survey 1850; funded 1853, last of the Bay lights
evidence.quote: As early as 1850 the U.S. Coast Survey had recommended that a lighthouse be constructed at this critical location.
Point Bonita Lighthouse was not funded by Congress until 1853
The largest wreck to occur in the vicinity of Point Bonita was that of the sidewheeler steamship Tennessee on March 6, 1853.
Congress had finally authorized and appropriated $25,000 for the Point Bonita Lighthouse just three days before the wreck on March 3, 1853.

On September 29, 1854 a petition was submitted to the Secretary of the Treasury from the Branch Pilots Association and Merchant Ship Masters urging that there be no more delay in the construction of the lighthouse.

Finally, on November 15, 1854 — more than a year and a half after Congress appropriated funding — the lighthouse inspector of the 12th Lighthouse District received authority to solicit contracts for the light's construction.
The work was completed by local contractors and the Point Bonita Lighthouse beamed its first rays out to sea on May 2, 1855.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Cannon dates differ: Aug 1855 (Putnam, quoting the order to Sgt Malony; LighthouseFriends 8 Aug), July 1855 borrowed (Bulletin 1915), Aug 1856 (NRHP). End: fall 1857 (Putnam, Bulletin) or 18 March 1858 (NRHP). Bell: 1856 (Putnam) or 1858 (NRHP). Gun 24-pounder (Putnam) or 10-pounder (Bulletin).
1855 is the first tower and lens; 1877 is the brick base at the lower site to which the 1855 lantern and lens were moved.

notes_for_editor: LighthouseFriends dates the snow-day fog signal to 11 Dec 1931; the 1933 Bulletin says 1932 (used). LighthouseFriends credits Keeper George D. Cobb with a Dec 1896 silver-medal rescue, but the USLHS roster has Cobb at Point Bonita only 1900-04 (second then first assistant); left out as unverified. NRHP says transferred to NPS 1981 vs LighthouseFriends 'owned by Coast Guard, scheduled for transfer'. Roster lists USCG crew after 1960 and head keepers Hogenmiller/Belisle/Coy/Wilson etc. from LighthouseFriends; post-1960 names left out of the roster by the living-people rule except Van Buskirk, who is named in a published press account. Roster lines 'Franklin E. Swanson (1950s-)' and 'Franklin P. Swanson (1947-)' kept as printed. Page numbers for LSS 1894/1895 and Putnam are scan pages; printed numbers are marked uncertain (?) by corpus.py. Cannon in NRHP list says 1855-1857 in one place and installed Aug 1856 in another. Tunnel Chinese-labour detail is LighthouseFriends only. Wikipedia not used. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Putnam gives 306 ft for the first tower, NRHP and LighthouseFriends 260 ft (now stated in the story). Putnam's elevation passage is printed p.140 (scan 189), the fog-gun passage pp.125-126.
